played: I played GLACIER SLIDE (rime-2) through the real flow - title, NEW GAME, unlock, and the real course loader - across about twenty-five headless sessions, driving real KeyboardEvents and screenshotting every event. Route: (1) BEAT 1, the summit shelf: read the GLACIER SLIDE board from the spawn pad and again from a metre away, walked to both pedestals and the LUGE race pad, stood still four seconds beside the bumbler's patrol loop, then held W on the authored spawn facing to see where the course sends you. (2) BEAT 2, the flume: rode the upper run from the chute mouth three separate ways (steering at each deck point, holding the crouch the sign asks for, and looking one point ahead), jumped GAP A on its own eleven times, ran the TURN 3 ice wheel eleven times at four course-clock phases three ways - plain, crouched and jumping - dropped onto one of its arms to see whether it can really be ridden, then rode the lower run from the mesa lip and jumped GAP B and GAP C. Measured what crouching at speed on ice actually does against the same stretch without it. (3) BEAT 3/4, the lake and the west ice face: spawned at cp-lake, walked 20 m west to the foot of the face, waited for the ice lift at the bottom of its travel and rode it up and back down, then attacked the four static seracs nineteen times with every jump technique I could produce. (4) BEAT 5, the crystal cavern: walked in from the apron through the beam lanes, stood in lane 1 for six seconds, pounded the crystal and climbed the vanish stair, looked at the Warden in its room. (5) BEAT 6, the crevasse: crossed the vanish snow bridges from the approach ledge three times at three run-ups, stood under the hanging icicle, dropped to the shaft floor and tried to wall-kick out four times - twice hammering the button, twice with a disciplined rhythm - sampling every 55-60 ms. (6) BEAT 8, the peak: walked the trodden path from the shelf toward the peak, then tried ROUTE A's serac spiral twenty-four times from block 1, and finally teleported to the cap to check the crest itself collects. Along the way I measured a twelve-point table of how far a jump actually travels against how long W is held, because every climb on this course turned on it. THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION I WAS ASKED: on this course ice is LOST CONTROL, not lost grip. On the upper flume you keep steering authority and the ice just carries you wide - that would be lost grip - but the TURN 1 berm stops 6.6 m before the corner does, so the drift has nothing to catch it and every ride ended 14 m below on the glacier. On the lower flume it is worse: the 21.6-degree head pitch is over TUNE.slope.iceSlideDeg, so you are in slopeSlide at the 16 m/s slide cap within a second of touching the lip, where the stick does not steer at all, and TURN 5 arrives six metres later. The player never gets an input that matters.

defects.where: rime-2 BEAT 1 -> BEAT 2, from the start position (0, 30, -26) on the authored spawn facing yaw -2.58, to the chute mouth U0 (4, 29.4, -22)
defects.did: held W and nothing else, on the facing the game itself hands you at the start. No camera work, no jump. This is the most literal reading of the course's own sign: THE CHUTE ONLY GOES DOWN.
defects.happened: the hero ran 5 m, clipped the extreme south-west corner of the flume's mouth deck and walked straight off the side of the mountain: trail (3.2, 30.1, -20.9) run -> (5.2, 28.5, -17.7) FALLING -> hardLand at (10.2, 5.1, -9.6). A 25 m fall in under 3 s, no death, no checkpoint - and the entire 120 m flume, the race, and 5 of the 8 beats are now above you. The way back is the whole course.
defects.should: walking forward off the start pad should feed the hero onto the ice. The authored spawn (0,30,-30) does aim at the middle of the mouth, but the game boots at checkpoints[0] (0,30,-26), 4 m closer to the lip, on the SAME yaw - and from there the same heading crosses the deck's near edge 0.76 of the way to its south-west corner and runs out of deck immediately.

defects.where: rime-2 BEAT 2, the ice wheel at TURN 3 (rotor [33, 21.90, -24.5], arms 2, len 4.2, period 4.4; deck top 20.60, chute 5.20 m wide)
defects.did: ran the deck through the wheel from a safe start 5 m short of it, at four course-clock phases, three ways - plain run, run holding crouch, and run with a jump timed at the bar
defects.happened: 7 of 11 attempts ended in a CRUSH death (cause 'crush'): run@1.1 at [32.04, 21.04, -23.02]; run@3.3 at [32.02, 21, -23.66]; crouch@0.0 at [32.02, 20.96, -24.25]; crouch@1.1 at [32.02, 21.01, -23.58]; crouch@3.3 at [32.04, 21.04, -23.06]; jump@1.1 at [34.49, 22.14, -26.65]; jump@3.3 at [34.67, 22.14, -26.64]. The arms are 4.2 m long, so the swept disc is 8.4 m across on a 5.2 m chute - it covers the deck from berm to berm, there is no lane past it, and the bar's underside sits about 1.05 m over a deck a 1.50 m hero is standing on.
defects.should: the course comment promises 'a RIDEABLE solid... a timing puzzle, not a trap'. Death by crush from a decorative-looking ice bar on a slick 14-degree ramp, where the player has just committed to a jump, is a trap. Either the arms should shove/carry on contact or the bar needs enough clearance to duck.
defects.note: proven separately: dropping ONTO an arm does work - the hero stands on it and is carried round (33.06,22.15,-26.71) -> (30.79,22.15,-24.46)

defects.where: rime-2 BEAT 2, the mid station on the east mesa - the PEDESTAL at (36, 17, -6) (kind pedestal, mat 'ice', tint ICE, glow AURORA), beside the cp-mesa checkpoint 2 m away

On a glacier at 17 m, in a course whose palette is snow-white, ice-blue and gold, it reads like a piece of meadow was dropped on the mountain. defects.where: rime-2 BEAT 6, THE WALL-KICK SHAFT at (-13, -21): floor 14.40, exit ledge 23.00, 3.20 m clear, 8.80 m tall
defects.did: climbed it four separate times from the shaft floor - twice hammering Space at every wall contact (29 and 28 kicks fired), once with a disciplined rhythm (jump, hold into the wall, ONE Space the instant the hero grabs it, respect the 0.28 s lockout, alternate walls), sampling every 55-60 ms throughout

This shaft is the ONLY way out of the crevasse and the required line to cp5, sigil 7 and the seracs back up to the summit shelf; a player who drops in and cannot kick out is in a hole with no exit and no death to reset him.

defects.where: rime-2 - the climb back, every beat of it: BEAT 4 west ice face (2.42-2.87 m steps at +2.40 m), BEAT 7 east serac spiral (3.14 m), BEAT 8 ROUTE A (3.90 m at +1.45 m)
defects.did: measured what a jump actually covers: stood on the flat lake ice and jumped twelve times with run-ups of 0, 90, 150, 220, 300 and 450 ms, single and double, recording launch speed and the distance travelled before landing
defects.happened: a SINGLE jump covers 2.62 m from a standing start and 2.89 - 3.25 m off any run-up a small block allows (measured launch speeds only reach about 3 m/s on the flat). A DOUBLE covers 4.53 - 6.50 m. ROUTE A's required 3.90 m step sits in the dead zone BETWEEN them: the single lands 0.4 - 0.8 m short (which is exactly where three of my ROUTE A attempts ended, at (3.88, 33.90, -47.95)) and the double flies 1 - 5 m past it. The west face is the mirror problem - its steps are only 2.42-2.87 m apart but rise 2.40 m, so the single cannot make the height (apex 1.91 m) and the double, which can, travelled 7.6 m at a 2.87 m target and put the hero on the ground 9 m below.
defects.should: a required stair over an 11 m drop should be inside one move's envelope with margin, not between two moves' envelopes. This is one number away from working: bring ROUTE A's step down toward 3.2 m, or widen the blocks so the landing has slack.
defects.note: the distances also scatter badly - two of twelve measurements came out at 5.94 m and 21.60 m with the same inputs as neighbours that gave 3.12 m and 4.53 m, so the same key press does not reliably produce the same hop

defects.where: rime-2 BEAT 6, the vanish snow bridges - approach ledge (-25.4, top 17.60, -7.8) then four snow slabs 3.16 m apart at +0.60 m (tops 17.80 / 18.40 / 19.00 / 19.60), cycle on 3.2 off 1.8 warn 0.7, phases 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5, with 11 m of air underneath

defects.happened: the best crossing reached bridge 2 of 4 and then fell into the hollow on bridge 3 (deaths 0 -> 1). The run-ups either side of 200 ms do not miss by a little, they miss by everything: 120 ms of W moved the hero 0.8 m against a 3.26 m step and left him standing on the ledge, and 300 ms threw him 10 m past bridge 1 to (-15.78, 4.93, -10.51), on the floor of the hollow.
defects.should: a bridge line over an 11 m drop should have a landing window you can feel. Here the window between 'the jump does not move you' and 'the jump throws you off the far end' is about a tenth of a second of held W.

defects.where: rime-2, the movement itself, measured on this course - it is what makes every climb in BEATS 4, 6, 7 and 8 feel unfair
defects.did: measured jump distance against how long W was held before the jump, on flat lake ice and again on the crevasse ledge
defects.happened: the distance a jump covers is hypersensitive to a few tens of milliseconds of run-up. On the crevasse ledge: 120 ms of W = 0.8 m travelled, 200 ms = a clean 3.2 m landing, 300 ms = 10 m and a death. On the lake: standing still = 2.62 m, and the twelve-measurement table scatters (two of twelve came out at 5.94 m and 21.60 m with the same inputs as neighbours that gave 3.12 m and 4.53 m). There is no walk-speed hop: the smallest jump a keyboard can produce is 2.62 m.
defects.should: a platformer whose stairs are 2.4-3.9 m apart needs a hop the player can aim. Either the analog ramp needs a real walk band you can hold, or every climb on this course needs to be built for the jump that actually exists.
defects.note: this is the single root cause behind the west ice face, ROUTE A, the snow bridges and (probably) the east serac spiral all failing

defects.where: rime-2, the slopeSlide animation - seen on the spire's south face, on the shelf's north skirt at (3.2, 30.7, -38.1), and on the glacier under the flume
defects.did: fell off the flume and off the shelf several times and watched the hero slide
defects.happened: slopeSlide renders as a scarecrow: arms straight out to the sides just below horizontal, legs straight and apart, torso bolt upright, no lean, no crouch, no edge. It reads as an un-posed T-pose, and it is the pose the player spends most of his time in on this course because every fall ends in a long slide. The run and jump poses in the same session are properly animated, so it is this state specifically.
defects.should: a slide down a 40-degree ice face wants a braced, leaning, low pose - the hero should look like he is fighting it

defects.where: rime-2, the spire's shadowed flanks - the south face below the shelf and the north skirt between the shelf and the peak
defects.did: slid down the south face after walking off the shelf, and walked north toward the peak

In _shots/play_rime2_shelf/03_03_sign_close.png the entire frame is that flat dark field with no horizon and no landmark - the player is moving at speed and can see nothing but a wall. In _shots/play_rime2_peak/02_A1_route_a_foot.png the slope you are about to climb is darker than the sky behind it.
defects.should: CONTRACT section 15's readability law asks for the walked surface to be at least 3.5:1 against the fog band behind it; here the walked surface is the darker of the two, and it is snow

worked: rime-2 loads from the Keep flow (title -> NEW GAME -> unlockAll -> goto) and drops the hero on the summit shelf at [0, 30, -26], grounded on snow

rime-2 loads through the real flow (title -> NEW GAME -> unlockAll -> __dev.goto) and spawns grounded on the summit shelf at (0, 30, -26), surface snow, HUD live (coins 0/100, 8 sigil pips, CHECKPOINT 0/4)
the GLACIER SLIDE board is legible from the spawn pad without walking to it - big header, good contrast on the cream plate

standing completely still for 4 s beside the shelf bumbler's patrol loop moved the hero 0.00 m - the patroller does not shove an idle player (this was a real defect on this shelf once and it is fixed)

the flume itself looks superb in motion (shot 02_E1_forward_4.png): big ice deck panels with bright cream leading-edge stripes, ice pylons carrying it over the glacier, coin arcs tracing the racing line, and the pinnacle and the lake read clearly in the distance
a 25 m fall off the shelf is a hardLand, not a death - the course's 'there is no fall damage, the punishment is the climb' promise holds (deaths stayed 0)
GAP A (4.84 m gap in the upper flume) clears with one timed jump off a running approach - landed at [31.99, 21.13, -21.99]
you really can RIDE the ice wheel - dropping onto an arm leaves the hero standing on it and carried round ([33.06, 22.15, -26.71] -> [30.79, 22.15, -24.46])

you really can RIDE the ice wheel: dropping onto the top of an arm from 1 m up leaves the hero standing on it, grounded, and carried a quarter turn round ((33.06, 22.15, -26.71) -> (30.79, 22.15, -24.46) in 3.4 s)
GAP A, the 4.84 m gap in the upper flume, clears with one timed Space off the running deck approach - landed on U3 at (31.99, 21.13, -21.99)
death and respawn on the flume is fast and clean: the dev panel read respawn 513 ms and the hero was back on the cp-summit pad, upright and controllable
the checkpoint is unmistakable at distance: the lit pad throws a tall teal light column you can see from anywhere on the mesa, and the HUD pip updates to CHECKPOINT 1/4 the moment you touch it
the shelf bumbler and the mesa bumbler are readable, charming and clearly non-lethal - a green waddler in a bowler hat that stands beside the checkpoint and does not attack
GAP C on the lower flume clears with a single timed jump (landed [12.58, 5.42, 19.01])
the open crest on the peak collects on contact and fires the course-clear flow (crests 1 -> 1, state clear)
the open crest on the peak collects the moment you touch it and fires the course-clear flow (game state went to 'clear')
the cp-lake checkpoint loads and spawns cleanly on the frozen lake at (3.73, 1, 25.54), and walking 20 m west across the lake ice to the foot of the west face arrived within 0.10 m of the target
the cavern beam lanes really kill - standing in lane 1 died within 6 s (deaths 2 -> 3)

the crystal cavern beam lanes really are lethal - standing on the cavern floor in lane 1 died inside 6 s, and walking in from the mouth toward the crystal also died on a beam, so they are a hazard and not decoration

the vanish crystal stair (step 1: 1.6 m across, +1.35 m) DOES land, with ['0 ms single', '70 ms single'] (six techniques tried: 0/70/130/170/200/280 ms of W, single and double, releasing W before the jump)

the west-face ice lift works exactly as an elevator should: standing on the block at the bottom carried the hero from y 3.12 up to 12.70 and back down again, grounded the whole way - the quick way up to the cavern apron is solid
the four vanish snow bridges' first two slabs cross cleanly with a 200 ms run-up and one hop each, and the snow-white slabs with cream leading-edge stripes read well against the blue hollow
blocked: The two hanging icicles over the lower flume (pendulums at (34.6, 19.6, 2.0) and (22, 13.6, 18.1)) - I could never get the hero to STAND under one. The deck there is the 21.6-degree head of the lower run, so every placement went into slopeSlide and left the flume before the icicle came round. Their kill capsules do sit on the deck line (measured: pendA capsule centres y 15.97 and 14.68 against a deck at 15.60; pendB y 10.50 and 9.45 against a deck at 7.53, which is 1.9 to 3.0 m ABOVE a 1.5 m hero's head and looks like it may never touch him) - somebody should check pendB specifically.
The breakable 'wrong-coloured wall' on the outside of TURN 5, the secret chute behind it, and the pinnacle cap with sigil 3 - never reached, because both flume runs threw me off before TURN 5.

The Warden of the crystal cavern - confirmed alive in its room with hp 3 and one kill volume, but never fought: I died on the beam lanes walking in, and the vanish stair to the roof was only cleared one step.
GAP B on the lower flume - never isolated cleanly, because I could not stay on the deck long enough to arrive at it at a sensible speed. GAP A and GAP C both pass with one timed jump.
The LUGE race crest (start pad (4, 30, -23) to finish (-4.5, 1, 27) in 45 s) - not completed, for the same reason: no ride of mine reached the lake on the ice.
BEAT 7, the east serac spiral, and the peak's ROUTE B ice lift and ROUTE C north spur - not driven; I spent the budget on ROUTE A because the course calls it the route that always works.
The melt pool dive, the heaving floes, the geyser jump pad, the ice fall and the sigils - outside my assigned area (the chute and the climb back), left for the lake/water lane.
